posts.title: Using AI Isn't Lazy. I Just Changed Jobs.
posts.description: A few friends keep calling me lazy for how much I use AI. I get why. From the outside, it looks like I talk to my computer and the work just shows up. They're missing the point. Getting AI to do work at the quality I'd do it myself is hard. I'm not working less. I'm working more. I just have a different job now. Why it looks lazy from the outside Most of us judge effort by what we can see.

posts.title: I Replaced My GitHub Actions Bill With Broken MacBooks
posts.description: My GitHub Actions bill was over $1,000 a month. I replaced it with about $1,000 of used M1 Macs, most of them MacBooks with cracked screens from eBay. That's roughly $12,000 a year back in my pocket, and the builds run on hardware I own. I first mentioned this in a reply on X back in August. It got about 250,000 views, which tells me a lot of developers are staring at the same bill.

posts.title: Don't Tell Your Customers You Don't Trust Them
posts.description: Business Lesson 101: don't tell your customers you don't trust them. It sounds too obvious to write down. Yet businesses do it every single day, usually with a straight face and a policy to point at. Years of good business, undone by one text I've used the same car detailer for years. When I started with him, it was basically a guy with a truck. I'd text him. He'd show up and make my cars look new
